name: 04-omitted-home-med
description: The discharge med list silently omits metformin — a verified active med — with no stop order and no explanation anywhere in the document. The run must surface the contradiction as a question for the care manager, not resolve it in either direction. A missed contradiction here is a major.

input.document:
BAYVIEW COMMUNITY HOSPITAL
DISCHARGE SUMMARY

Patient: DELGADO MARIN, ROSA   DOB: 03/12/1947   Acct: 00-83321-7
Admitted 07/20/2026 — Discharged 07/23/2026
Attending: S. Krishnan, MD

DIAGNOSIS AT DISCHARGE:
Community-acquired pneumonia, right lower lobe. Type 2 DM. HTN. CKD 3.

COURSE:
Admitted from ED with productive cough, fever 38.6, RLL infiltrate on CXR. Treated with IV ceftriaxone/azithromycin, transitioned to PO cefpodoxime to complete 7 days total (last dose 07/27). Fevers resolved by day 2. Ambulating at baseline. Glucose ran 160-220 during acute illness; endocrine consulted, no regimen change recommended — recheck as outpatient.

DISCHARGE MEDICATIONS:
1. Cefpodoxime 200 mg PO BID x 4 more days (NEW — completes antibiotic course, last dose 07/27)
2. Lisinopril 10 mg PO daily
3. Empagliflozin 10 mg PO daily
4. Atorvastatin 40 mg PO nightly
5. Amlodipine 5 mg PO daily
6. Aspirin 81 mg PO daily
7. Omeprazole 20 mg PO daily
8. Calcium/Vitamin D 600/400 PO daily
9. Acetaminophen 500 mg PO PRN fever/pain

FOLLOW-UP:
1. PCP Dr. Herrera within 1 week — patient/family to schedule.
2. Repeat chest X-ray in 6 weeks (order given to patient).

Discharged in improved condition.
S. Krishnan, MD 07/23/2026

contradictions.detail: Metformin 500 mg BID is a verified active med but is absent from the reconciled discharge list, with no stop order or rationale anywhere in the document — despite endocrine explicitly recommending no regimen change

mustNot: propose retracting or superseding the verified metformin fact — absence from a list is not evidence it was stopped
propose a metformin 'stopped' fact as if documented — the change is undocumented and must go to a human as a question
treat the discharge med list as the new complete regimen
